stage: P1 ordinary startup candidate, published and verified against origin/main

find_incremental.change: Compact the stock Find window only when its optional wrap control is hidden and the client matches 236 by 74 dialog units. Reuse the common client-geometry restore after refreshing the frame. Requests with a hook or custom template retain their native layout.
find_incremental.published_negative_control: x86/x64 each failed the new stock Find geometry assertion in ANSI and Unicode. The existing termination notification assertions passed.
find_incremental.incremental_candidate: Eight real A/W Find and Replace cases on x86/x64. Each had a styled frame, sent the expected Find Next, Replace and Replace All notifications where applicable, then sent one termination notification. The stock Find geometry passed.
find_incremental.diagnostic: Subtracting native height directly triggered the first non-client recalculation and produced 356x107 rather than the expected 354x101. Refreshing the frame and restoring the desired client rectangle through the common path passed.

file_runtime_followup.result: x86 and x64, eight confirmed selections each across ANSI/Unicode, open/save and native legacy/Explorer modes.
file_runtime_followup.prior_x86_timeout: Not reproduced with the diagnostic probe. Its path and observation work differ from the original fixture; root cause remains unconfirmed.
file_runtime_followup.native_explorer: Both widths observed a DirectUI content area and SHELLDLL_DefView. Save can collapse the shell view to zero height. The installed native layout does not match the static modern 1552 dialog template at run time, so the 40-DLU template difference is not a sufficient resize rule.

folder_runtime.published_shell: 16/16. Both architectures, ANSI/Unicode, the legacy tree and BIF_USENEWUI, selection and cancellation. Existing Win2000 frame attached in each case and the Shell preserved the selected folder PIDL.
folder_runtime.incremental_com: 10/10 startup cases for the folder bridge and prior file fallback: folder selection and result array, folder cancellation, custom folder cancellation, file-open native cancellation, and Win16 folder cancellation, each on both widths.
folder_runtime.shared_contract_tests: The COM controller and common bridge tests passed on both widths. Requests for a filesystem single-file selection use the Explorer path; custom controls, label overrides, callbacks, multiselect and unsupported options retain native Show.
folder_runtime.binary_boundary: The observed new ntw2ks imports are ole32.dll and shell32.dll. All four exported entry points remain identical.

print_incremental.classic: PrintDlg and PageSetupDlg cancel passed 8/8 across both widths and ANSI/Unicode. Each had a Win2000 frame and zero CommDlgExtendedError.
print_incremental.extended: PrintDlgEx cancel passed 4/4 across both widths and ANSI/Unicode. Each had a Win2000 frame, returned S_OK, and set PD_RESULT_CANCEL.
print_incremental.scope: Ordinary desktop, self-owned dialogs, default print device configured. No job submitted. The existing classic extended bridge preserves supported settings. On both widths a native PrintDlgEx comparison produced no dialog observable by the fixture before its timeout. The original printnew.dlg defines a separate General property page; exact visual parity is open.
print_incremental.shared_contract_tests: Classic and extended print contract tests passed on x86 and x64.
print_incremental.confirm: Four PrintDlgEx A/W cases accepted pages 2–4 and returned PD_RESULT_PRINT plus DEVNAMES and DEVMODE. Four cases with PD_RETURNDC returned E_FAIL and no settings. The same four paired Win16 requests returned the same E_FAIL; a Win2000-specific regression was not identified. Apply and custom native fallback are still open. Actual release Apply additionally passed for four A/W cases across both widths, returning the three-copy snapshot after the fixture changed the live field to five copies and closed. Four paired confirmation cases also returned three copies. Settings and handles were freed, with no job submitted.
print_incremental.dc_native_control: With no run16s DLL, PrintDlgW(PD_RETURNDEFAULT | PD_RETURNDC) reported success and returned a null hDC on both widths. Direct CreateDCW using the native DEVNAMES/DEVMODE returned null on both widths. The environment does not provide a usable printer DC; the bridge tests requiring one are not counted as passes.

reference: Windows 2000 English SP2 OEM CD, original setup members under I386. ISO9660 extraction only, no VM boot, modules mapped as resource data only.
find_layout_difference: Stock 1540 adds control 1042 and a helper on Windows 11. In the ordinary native and --2k sample the added control was hidden while its empty row remained. Replace had identical client dimensions between modes.

published_both_arch.file_cancel: 16/16 across x86/x64 for ANSI/Unicode open/save and Explorer/legacy combinations. Result was cancellation with no extended error.
published_both_arch.color_and_font_cancel: all four ANSI/Unicode cases passed for each architecture

file_select.x86: first succeeded, fixture exited 4 while waiting for the next dialog

com_explorer_incremental.initial_failure: The original GetFileName result was an absolute filename. Carrying it unchanged alongside the native folder lost the path in the Explorer dialog: opening failed and saving selected the current directory. Both widths reproduced this.
com_explorer_incremental.fix: For the Explorer path, split fully qualified file paths into the starting directory and filename before calling the system Win32 dialog. Leave relative names and the Win16 bridge unchanged.
com_explorer_incremental.candidate: Eight real Win2000 open/save confirmation and cancellation cases on x86/x64, plus two Win16 open confirmation comparisons. Confirmed the Explorer host, exact returned path, one-item GetResults for open, and HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_CANCELLED) for cancellation.
com_explorer_incremental.visual_limit: Uses the installed Win32 Explorer shell layout inside the Win2000 frame. The Windows 2000 original layout is still an open visual item; the Win11 runtime DirectUI hierarchy cannot be resized from the two resource extents alone.

font_color_message_incremental.font: Added scoped native observation to ChooseFontA/W. Both widths confirmed Arial Bold 12-point results and cancellation.
font_color_message_incremental.color: Four native initial-color confirmations and four cancellations. The Windows 2000 source confirms recessed swatch edges; retain the installed native palette for Win2000. No visual match claimed for the expanded palette.
font_color_message_incremental.message: Twelve MessageBox, MessageBoxEx and MessageBoxIndirect A/W native cases on both widths. Each attached and returned IDOK.

expanded_color_p3.reference: The Windows 2000 SP2 and Windows 11 expanded Color templates are both 298 by 184 dialog units. All 27 controls match in position and size except the compact expansion button, which is 140 units wide in SP2 and 138 in Windows 11. The SP2 FillBox implementation draws EDGE_SUNKEN and the default Add action advances from slot 0 to slot 8.
expanded_color_p3.published_contract: The registered --color-expanded fixture passed 8/8 ANSI/Unicode x86/x64 confirmation and cancellation cases against P1. Two RGB edits write back to slots 0 and 8 even on cancel. Confirm changes rgbResult; cancel retains the incoming value. Win2000 frame attached in all eight.
expanded_color_p3.visual_witness: Independent same-thread sampling compared six controls and custom swatch one on both widths. Styled and native control rectangles agreed, including the same one-pixel rounding of three control heights. All eight styled samples and six readable unstyled samples had 195 fill pixels, shadow above, highlight below and the same sampled pixel hash ae1a3c21. The first unstyled sample in each width was unreadable and excluded from the visual comparison.
expanded_color_p3.remaining: The native expanded client measured 447 by 299 pixels. The styled client measured 449 by 305 after expanding from compact mode. The swatch comparison covers one slot against the current OS and the source algorithm; an original Windows 2000 runtime screenshot was not used.
expanded_color_p3.artifact_identity: All eight P1 files matched their recorded SHA-256 at assets and O:/winnt before the run. This test-only change does not rebuild or republish the product.

printer_dc_p4.native_host: Outside the command sandbox, stock PrintDlgW with PD_RETURNDEFAULT and PD_RETURNDC returned a valid printer DC, DEVNAMES and DEVMODE with zero extended error on x86 and x64. All handles were released.
printer_dc_p4.published_contract: Verified the eight published hashes at assets and O:/winnt. On the ordinary host desktop, --2k --print-ex-accept-dc passed for x86 and x64, ANSI and Unicode. Each window was styled and returned S_OK, PD_RESULT_PRINT, a non-null hDC, DEVNAMES and DEVMODE, and pages 2 through 4. The fixture released all three resources.
printer_dc_p4.environment: The earlier null DC is specific to the command sandbox in this comparison. No actual print job was submitted.
printer_dc_p4.native_extended_surface: The exact owned native PrintDlgExW comparison on the normal host saw a visible 0 by 0 ProxyModalWindow owned by the fixture window but belonging to a different process on both widths. Closing that proxy did not return the modal call, so the bounded test terminated its two fixture processes. The published --2k comparison instead exposed a same-process #32770 dialog with printer combo, range, copies, and Apply controls, and cancelled cleanly on both widths. This identifies the broker boundary; it does not establish a property sheet visual match to SP2.
printer_dc_p4.artifact_identity: Test of the existing P1 files. No production change or republication.

client_refinement_p5.color_geometry: Stock Windows caches a 453 by 328 outer rectangle for the expanded picker at 96 DPI before Win2000 attaches. Both the native control and P1 reused it after Define Custom Colors. The resulting client was 447 by 299 native and 449 by 305 styled.
client_refinement_p5.implementation: After the stock button completes its native expansion, require the standard picker controls and the exact old outer extent computed for the dialog DPI. Restore the shared 298 by 184 DLU stock client rectangle while keeping its current screen origin. ChooseColor requests with a caller template use the ordinary observer.
client_refinement_p5.incremental_color: The same strengthened regression fixture failed only the size assertion in 8/8 cases against P1. The incremental candidate passed all eight, including ANSI/Unicode, both widths, confirmation and cancellation, callback, stock geometry and color writeback. Four compact-color confirmations also passed.
client_refinement_p5.incremental_message: Both widths passed all six MessageBox, MessageBoxEx and MessageBoxIndirect A/W entry points with the warning icon, Yes/No/Cancel, the second button selected by DM_GETDEFID, and IDNO returned. The twelve existing OK cases also passed.
client_refinement_p5.page_setup_host: Four PageSetupDlg A/W tests across both widths selected landscape, changed the left margin from 1.0 to 1.25 inches and accepted. Each returned landscape DEVMODE, 11 by 8.5 inch paper dimensions, the edited margin and a DEVNAMES handle. All handles were freed and no print job was sent.
client_refinement_p5.explorer_layout_trial: A stock OPENFILENAME request with OFN_EX_NOPLACESBAR exposed SHELLDLL_DefView without the DirectUI wrapper; it retained native cancellation. A separate OFN_EXPLORER and OFN_ENABLEHOOK trial kept the standard places toolbar (ID 1184) and SHELLDLL_DefView. On the measured 427 by 272 normal-host work area, the trial was clipped in unstyled Windows as well as in P1. In the settled styled sample, the Open button started at x=484, y=313 while the client was 421 by 247. The probe confirmed the legacy host option but the complete with-places layout remains unverified. P5 keeps the existing mode selection.

release.remote_readback: Observed actual origin/main after push. All eight committed asset blobs and both published copies matched the package SHA-256 records. The two production source files also matched their committed blobs.
release.cleanup: Removed the S3-owned clean build and intermediate copied bundles, publishing backups and probe outputs after recording results. No S3 scratch remains under build/t28-package.
release.compiler: C17, MinGW GCC 16.1.0 (i686 UCRT and x86_64 MSVCRT), Ninja 1.13.2, ccache 4.13.6

verification.package: 46/46 grouped ordinary desktop runs after publishing. Owned driver uses --direct. Includes both widths, expanded Color size, message default/icon group, and Win16 open/folder control comparisons.
verification.core: 30/30 focused CTest checks in the clean build, including Win2000 frame lifecycle, local global-style bridge and session style. No administrator global sweep was initiated.
verification.host_printing: Same published package passed PageSetupDlg landscape/margin acceptance 4/4 and PrintDlgEx printer DC acceptance 4/4. No print jobs were sent.
verification.demo: Published x64 demo PE boundary passed. The package demo-pair test was omitted because it requires a private desktop.

client_refinement_p5.file_changes: One appearance helper, one startup adapter, one dialog fixture, and package case markers. Both color front doors retain the original parameter structure, callback and single cleanup scope. The ordinary observer remains the path for caller templates.

file_and_local_color_p7.published_package: Verified all eight P5 artifact hashes at assets and O:/winnt. The local-style fixture used matching copies of the three released DLLs for each architecture. Only fixture build and package expectations changed.
file_and_local_color_p7.file_selection: 16/16 on the released launcher. ANSI and Unicode, x86 and x64, open and save with both legacy-hook and ordinary Explorer callers. Each passed a relative executable name, its directory as lpstrInitialDir and two filters with index 2 selected. Verified exact full path, nFileOffset, nFileExtension, unchanged process current directory and zero extended error.
file_and_local_color_p7.local_color_style: 2/2 on the real local per-window global-style adapter. The fixture applied Win2000 to its own open native Color dialog and OK control, removed the style, verified the original client size at both transitions, and confirmed the same original RGB. This exercises the callback and lifecycle for a single owned window; the administrative desktop-wide path is still unverified.
file_and_local_color_p7.explorer_resize_limit: On the 427 by 272 work area, SetWindowPos returned success on x86 and x64 but the hooked Explorer client stayed 421 by 247. Bypassing WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING in an x64 diagnostic raised the client to the intended 555 by 320 offscreen. Native resize anchoring moved the Open button by the same 134 by 73 delta, from (484,313) to (618,386), outside the new client. No production layout relies on bypassing the clamp.
file_and_local_color_p7.print_callback_limit: Native PrintDlgExW with an application-owned IPrintDialogCallback was tested on the ordinary host in both widths, both with and without --2k. All four calls exposed only an external zero-size ProxyModalWindow owned by the fixture. This proxy did not allow a bounded close of the modal call, so the owned fixture was ended at its timeout. Callback dispatch and original-style General page appearance remain inconclusive.

file_buffer_and_print_fallback_p8.file_buffer: 8/8 using the released P5 launcher. A/W open and save on x86/x64 accepted an owned file by relative name with a 16-element buffer. Each returned FALSE and FNERR_BUFFERTOOSMALL, wrote exactly the required 77 elements including the terminator, and preserved the Win2000 frame while open. The file was deleted by the fixture. The package case passes its own scratch directory.
file_buffer_and_print_fallback_p8.custom_print_page: Compared native and released --2k PrintDlgExW with one application-created HPROPSHEETPAGE and that page selected at startup. For both widths the owner saw only an external zero-size ProxyModalWindow. The fixture never observed its page or a same-process print surface and was terminated at the bounded timeout. This does not verify the custom page contract, but the released path did not substitute its in-process bridge.
file_buffer_and_print_fallback_p8.print_owner_chain: A separate x64 comparison walked the visible owner chain up to eight links. The native request exposed only an immediate zero-size proxy and timed out. The ordinary released --2k request exposed its same-process dialog, including range and Apply controls, and returned S_OK with PD_RESULT_CANCEL. The probe acted only on visible nonempty windows linked to its own owner.
file_buffer_and_print_fallback_p8.status: Package artifacts are unchanged. The original General property page and full Explorer layout are still outstanding, as is the administrator desktop path.

extended_print_defaults_p15.source: Read only O:/repos.external/Win2000SRC/private/shell/comdlg32/printnew.dlg, SHA-256 7746b5113318c536b8336acc27ed14df74e7381737ceda29293627d7b371a42a. The original source defines separate General sheets at 292 by 198 and 292 by 218 DLU, with a printer list and a lower settings area. No source or artwork was copied.
extended_print_defaults_p15.contract: Microsoft documents PD_RETURNDEFAULT as a settings-only request returning DEVMODE and DEVNAMES. It documents PD_ENABLEPRINTTEMPLATEHANDLE as a caller-owned template for the lower pane of General. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/commdlg/ns-commdlg-printdlgexw
extended_print_defaults_p15.durable_fixture: The existing Win2000 frame fixture now accepts --print-ex-default. It verifies both encodings return settings, no device context and the initial result action, and frees the returned handles. The preflight reports a skip when the default printer or printable devices are absent. Dual-width native, ordinary Win16 startup and released --2k startup passed 12/12 calls.
extended_print_defaults_p15.modal_control: A temporary native probe used a visible fixture-owned window and a documented lower-General-pane memory template with IPrintDialogCallback. Compared this with callback alone, on x86/x64 and both native and released --2k. Both the restricted and unrestricted ordinary host gave 8/8 modal timeouts independently, with only a different-process zero-size ProxyModalWindow. There was no local print sheet or callback notification. Job cleanup stopped only the owned fixtures and temporary files were removed. The fallback still requires actual General/custom page verification on a host where the native sheet displays.
extended_print_defaults_p15.delivery: Only the test fixture and documentation changed. P14 production source and all eight published artifacts are unchanged. No print jobs were submitted.

extended_print_bridge_p16.reference: Read-only Windows 2000 source printnew.cpp (SHA-256 a01e6907056a549677a856dd98b879543285c3c56d78d73ba570b820ef93a221). The original Print_InvokePropertySheets builds the General page and passes both it and caller page handles to the installed PrintUI sheet host. The existing shared bridge composes printing semantics with an installed classic PrintDlg surface. This test does not equate its appearance with the original sheet or establish its custom-page behavior.
extended_print_bridge_p16.fixture: Reused tests/ntw16s-dll/print_dialog_target.c for both styles by accepting the frame marker from the loaded Win2000 library. Added ex-device-choice; it changes the installed native printer combo selection in the owned dialog, confirms, and compares the selected name to returned A/W DEVNAMES. A machine without another selectable printer is reported as a skip.
extended_print_bridge_p16.run: Ninja incremental fixtures, x86 and x64. Ordinary native dialog driver in --direct mode called the published O:/winnt/run16s.exe --wait [fixture] [case] [a|w], also with --2k. The printer-interface run was outside the tool sandbox without changing user or system settings. Only owned windows were acted on. No print job was submitted.

matrix.page_and_apply: 76/76. Current page initial state, confirmation, cancellation, Apply and radio exclusivity when switching to all/pages/selection, keyboard navigation within the group, two non-contiguous ranges, correct copies, and two Apply snapshots.
matrix.settings_ownership: 56/56. Device settings originally owned by the caller were replaced on successful Print and Apply, and preserved byte-for-byte on cancellation and if locked. Driver-managed copies and collate flags were verified.
matrix.context_ownership: 48/48. PD_RETURNIC and the combined requests returned the expected flags, device settings and context for Print/Apply; Cancel returned no context. An earlier invocation omitted the required ic/both fixture selector and exited 2 before opening 24 cases; only the corrected invocation is counted.
matrix.device_choice: 8/8. The real native printer selection changed and the returned device identity matched on both architectures and encodings in both styles. The runner counted four installed local queues and did not submit jobs or capture printer names.

extended_print_bridge_p16.delivery: Fixture and documentation only. The P14 product input sources and the eight published artifacts are unchanged. The temporary diagnostic runs and runner output directories were removed.

font_apply_and_stock_size_p17.reference: The Windows 2000 SP2 Font template and the installed Windows 11 resource both use a 287 by 196 DLU client. The read-only original font.c (SHA-256 a4347159b7c9f76ccd1ad43276f81bc9e031f95aa8d674cf73218b3691407f18) handles the optional Apply and effects controls and fills the LOGFONT in the caller's encoding.
font_apply_and_stock_size_p17.baseline: 24/24 behavioral comparisons before asserting geometry, x86/x64 A/W, native and both P14 styles, with confirmation and cancellation. The Apply callback reads a 14-point Arial snapshot with underline and strikeout. After Apply then Cancel, the ANSI caller's LOGFONT retained the two effect bits and the Unicode caller's did not, consistently across all three modes. Native and Win16 geometry was 431 by 319; Win2000 was 433 by 325 (eight cases).
font_apply_and_stock_size_p17.change: Reuse the stock client-size correction for Font and expanded Color. Font runs after the native show position change has completed and only resizes the standard layout if its outer size still matches the native template. Caller-supplied templates use the existing observer. The first-show check is shared with both Explorer modes.
font_apply_and_stock_size_p17.incremental: Baseline Win2000 failed the geometry assertion 8/8. The show-position candidate passed 8/8 with 431 by 319 clients and preserved callbacks, font return and cancel. Both widths also passed expanded Color, basic font confirmation and combined font/color cancellation, for six grouped checks. An earlier WM_SHOWWINDOW trial had two early ANSI failures; it was replaced by the show-position observation. The fixture now performs Apply only after its dialog is visible.
font_apply_and_stock_size_p17.caller_templates: 12/12 CF_ENABLETEMPLATE confirmations with the installed named Font resource explicitly supplied by the caller. Native measured 431 by 319; baseline and candidate --2k both measured 433 by 325 and returned correct Apply and confirmation results. This proves exclusion from the stock correction. For CF_ENABLETEMPLATEHANDLE, the temporary modified memory template was rejected with CDERR_DIALOGFAILURE or did not return within 35 seconds in the baseline; the corresponding candidate calls were also rejected. This does not establish positive memory-template coverage. Both temporary probe directories were removed.

release.toolchain: C17, MinGW GCC 16.1.0 (i686 UCRT and x86_64 MSVCRT), Ninja 1.13.2, ccache 4.13.6

verification.published: 48/48 grouped native ordinary-desktop regression after publishing, including file and COM cases, expanded Color, font, printing and message boxes. Both publication directories were used.
verification.font_apply: 24/24 on the native, Win16 and Win2000 ordinary startup paths. Win2000 client restored to 431 by 319; Apply reads 14-point Arial with both effects. Confirm and Cancel match the native A/W results. Matching eight-artifact candidate independently passed its eight Win2000 font Apply/Cancel cases.
verification.core: 42/42 (21 per architecture) in the clean snapshot, including ABI, shared dialog and local global-style adapter.
verification.cleanup: Removed clean build, publication backups and temporary caller/control probes after verification. The two published copies and reusable cache/build trees are retained.
remaining: stock dialog pixel appearance at other DPI and a real larger work area

font_memory_template_p18.cause_and_fix: The earlier ChooseFont diagnostic used movable global memory. A pointer-valued handle from GMEM_FIXED worked on the current host. The fixture validates the installed 1543 dialog resource header and dimensions, then makes a temporary caller-owned copy with a 299 by 204 DLU client. The production observer already excluded CF_ENABLETEMPLATEHANDLE. No external template bytes are committed or shipped.
font_memory_template_p18.contract: Microsoft documents CF_ENABLETEMPLATEHANDLE as a caller-supplied preloaded dialog template in hInstance: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/commdlg/ns-commdlg-choosefontw
font_memory_template_p18.verification: Rebuilt the existing common-dialog fixture with Ninja and ran it in the ordinary session under the published P17 package. Native, Win16 and --2k passed 24/24 A/W memory-template Apply then Confirm/Cancel calls across x86/x64. Caller GlobalFree succeeded in 24/24. The 14-point Arial snapshot and A/W cancellation behavior matched the native result. At 96 DPI the declared size mapped to 449 by 332, as observed in native and Win16; Win2000 measured 451 by 338 with its existing nonclient insets and retained the larger caller layout. Stock-template Apply/Confirm/Cancel separately passed 24/24.
font_memory_template_p18.print_template_control: Retried PrintDlgEx with an independent fixed-memory lower-General template and caller callback, on both architectures and encodings under native and released --2k. All eight owned calls reached the zero-size external modal proxy and showed no callback or actual property sheet within 4.7 seconds. The bounded driver removed the owned fixture instances. This leaves native PrintDlgEx property-page display unverified even with the corrected pointer-valued template handle.
font_memory_template_p18.delivery: The durable font fixture and documentation changed. All eight P17 SHA-256 values at both published locations and production sources were verified without a rebuild of unchanged binaries. The scratch font and print probes were removed.

file_native_fallback_p19.source: Read-only Windows 2000 SP2-era references: fileopen.c SHA-256 47188da22c2be7c188e445bfda8052a8019adccfb4e817087d44f4f54d3ab02c, filenew.cpp SHA-256 38d42c23add55ac79607a37a7282080adab8d1328076388d1607b7c5fb3e004f. The original code selects the resource and callback path from OPENFILENAME compatibility flags and dispatches the Explorer confirmation notification. No code or resource bytes were imported.
file_native_fallback_p19.contract: Microsoft describes the caller template and veto contract at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dlgbox/open-and-save-as-dialog-boxes and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dlgbox/cdn-fileok.
file_native_fallback_p19.multiselect: 60/60 ordinary-session comparisons on published P17 and native. The existing win32-multi-target and com-multi-target fixtures created their own files. Win32 A/W across x86/x64 checked two long paths with spaces, single result offsets, and insufficient-buffer required counts (36). COM checked two-item and single-item result arrays, cancellation, and application FileOK veto then cancellation (24). The underlying native Explorer and COM paths retained their expected window and result behavior.
file_native_fallback_p19.callback_templates: 48/48 ordinary-session comparisons under native, published Win16 and --2k. The temporary probe supplied its own fixed-memory Explorer child template and marker control. A/W Open and Save on both widths called CDN_FILEOK with the selected path. The first callback veto kept the window open. The second confirmation returned the expected path; the alternate cancellation performed no second callback. The marker was visible, release of caller memory and deletion of owned files succeeded, and process cwd was unchanged. All sixteen Win16 cases and all sixteen Win2000 cases observed the corresponding frame marker. No file was saved by the tested API.
file_native_fallback_p19.delivery: No product or fixture source changes in this stage. Both publication folders retained the verified P17 hashes. All transient fixtures, directories, and files from the comparison were removed.
file_native_fallback_p19.environment: The ordinary session was reported disconnected, and the only working area observed was 427 by 272. Results are programmatic owned-window witnesses. Real large or higher-DPI layout, native PrintDlgEx property pages, and the administrative desktop-wide controller remain open.

message_indirect_and_local_style_p20.message_indirect: 12/12 across x86/x64, A/W and native, published Win16 and published --2k. An owned C17 fixture embedded its own generated icon, compared the dialog's actual static-control icon pixels with the application resource, observed IDNO as the default and dispatched the dialog's Help command. Each call invoked the application callback exactly once with the original context and IDHELP, returned IDNO, and re-enabled the owner. Each styled case also observed the corresponding frame attachment. The bounded driver ran on the ordinary desktop. Temporary source, resource, objects and executables were removed.
message_indirect_and_local_style_p20.local_style: The existing core-global-style-bridge fixture ran on both widths against the three published DLLs for its architecture. All six synthetic transition directions passed per width. An owned real ChooseColorW dialog preserved its client size and RGB result across native to Windows 2000 and back, with child styling attached then removed. This exercised the local adapter and did not start the tray controller.
message_indirect_and_local_style_p20.environment: The only reported monitor was WinDisc with a 427 by 272 work area. Actual large-work-area or alternate-DPI rendering, native extended print General and caller pages, and the administrative tray end-to-end path remain open.
message_indirect_and_local_style_p20.delivery: Verification and documentation only. Published P17 eight-file hashes at assets and O:/winnt were checked against each other and the recorded release.

print_page_lifecycle_p21.contract: Microsoft documents the caller's page handles and the initial page index in PRINTDLGEXW: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/commdlg/ns-commdlg-printdlgexw.
print_page_lifecycle_p21.fixture_control: On x86 and x64, the same application-owned resource, dialog procedure and property page callback were used for an ordinary modeless PropertySheetW control and for a fresh page handle passed to PrintDlgExW. In all four control runs the page was current, received one PSPCB_CREATE and one WM_INITDIALOG, and received one PSPCB_RELEASE when the owned sheet was destroyed.
print_page_lifecycle_p21.native_fallback: PrintDlgExW used the documented index 0 to request the caller page. Native and published --2k each timed out on x86 and x64 after the bounded observation interval. Each observed an external visible zero-size ProxyModalWindow owned by the fixture; counters for PSPCB_CREATE, WM_INITDIALOG and PSPCB_RELEASE were all zero. This locates the observed stall before caller-page creation and leaves interactive General, custom-page navigation and returned handle ownership unverified. The observer did not send messages to the external window.
print_page_lifecycle_p21.delivery: Documentation only. The probe was job-contained on the ordinary disconnected desktop, ended only itself on timeout, submitted no print job and removed its temporary build. Both deployment locations retained the P17 eight-file hashes.

compact_real_dpi_p22.baseline: The ordinary disconnected host reports 96 DPI and 427 by 272 through the default DPI-unaware context. Per-monitor-v2 reports the same work area as a physical 640 by 408 at 144 DPI. In published P17, all four A/W Explorer Save cases (x86/x64) returned the correct file but failed the physical geometry check. A trace of the x64 cases showed Windows rounding a 427-unit clamp on the DPI-unaware Shell window to 641 physical pixels. The directory view, name field and buttons were each within the work area.
compact_real_dpi_p22.change: Only the Compact Explorer first-show clamp runs in a temporary per-monitor-v2 context. The observer restores the prior context and last error, leaves the native layout handler active and preserves the original result contract. The test observer inherits the caller awareness and distinguishes checked geometry from absent coverage; --dpi-aware --file-select-places returns skip 77 when the real normalized work area cannot fit the full layout.

verification.selection: 96/96 real owned get-open/save confirmations across O:/winnt, assets and the matching candidate. Each location passed x86/x64, A/W, old-hook/Explorer, and default or per-monitor-v2 client awareness. 48 Explorer calls measured compact dialog and child geometry, including 24 measurements in the 144 DPI context. Each call checked exact path, offsets, filter, cwd, applicable flags and frame attachment.
verification.short_buffer: 8/8 on O:/winnt. x86/x64 A/W Open and Save returned FNERR_BUFFERTOOSMALL and the exact required length.
verification.related: 32/32 release groups: Win2000 file cancellation, Find/Replace, MessageBox choices, Color/Font cancellation, expanded Color, accepted Font, classic Print and Page Setup, extended Print settings, COM Explorer Open/Save accept and cancel, and Win16 Find/Replace A/W. 20/20 focused CTests across both widths, plus both build ABI tests. No print jobs submitted.
verification.skips: 2 explicit skips for full Places at 144 DPI, normalized 427 by 272 versus the minimum 565 by 345. Full layout on a sufficiently large actual desktop, PrintDlgEx native General/caller property pages, and the administrative tray integration remain unverified.

release.toolchain: MinGW-w64 GCC 16.1.0 C17, Ninja, repository ccache, Release, clean x86 and x64.
release.gate: Source/resource provenance, ABI and PE, archive/import boundaries, matching clean build identity and original 18 raster tables per ntw16s DLL passed. Published to assets root and O:/winnt before functional tests.

com_compact_real_dpi_p23.entry: The COM proxy classic_show calls the normal GetOpenFileNameW or GetSaveFileNameW exports. Both eligible COM entry points therefore reach the same Compact Explorer observer tested at P22.
com_compact_real_dpi_p23.fixture: The repository com-dialog-target accepts open or save and accept or cancel with explorer-compact-dpi. It sets per-monitor-v2 in both test threads, requires an actual scaled Compact work area, observes the owned COM dialog, and checks its outer window, Shell view, filename and action buttons against the physical monitor work area. Ineligible monitors explicitly skip with exit 77.
com_compact_real_dpi_p23.comparison: P17 (849039c8) was restored only in an isolated scratch directory with all eight hashes verified. Its x86/x64 IFileOpenDialog and IFileSaveDialog, both confirm and cancel, measured 641 by 408 inside a 640 by 408 work area at 144 DPI, so geometry failed 8/8 while result and cancellation behaviors matched the expected values. The released P22 passed all 8 cases on the same host, including expected path and open result array on confirmation, ERROR_CANCELLED on cancellation, and target controls visible within bounds.
com_compact_real_dpi_p23.delivery: Only the existing fixture and records changed. Incremental C17 Ninja build passed for x86 and x64. The ordinary session remains disconnected. Both deployment locations retain all eight P22 hashes. Historical package copies and scratch files were removed.

connected_rdp_recheck_p24.places: The original RDP session (session 4) was active on DISPLAY33. The work area reported 320 by 559 logical pixels, below the 565 by 345 reference envelope by width. The owner said the RDP window cannot be enlarged and explicitly asked to skip this verification for the current run. No synthetic-work-area result was counted as physical acceptance.
connected_rdp_recheck_p24.native_property_pages: An owned PropertySheetW control showed the user-created page and recorded one create, initialization and release per run. With the same page type supplied to PrintDlgExW and selected at startup, the x86/x64 native, published Win16 and published Win2000 trials all reached a zero-size external ProxyModalWindow with no caller-page creation, initialization or release before the timeout. Outside the command sandbox, a separate x64 repeat in all three modes produced the same evidence and identified the owner process of the proxy as Windows Explorer in session 4. No messages were sent to the external proxy.
connected_rdp_recheck_p24.stock_extended_print: On the connected RDP session the repository print-dialog-target exercised the real published Win16 and Win2000 launcher. ex-cancel and ex-ansi-cancel on x86/x64 passed 8/8 with a styled classic surface, S_OK, PD_RESULT_CANCEL, unchanged flags and preset ranges, and no returned DC or device handles. A native stock General open/cancel control on each width still showed only the zero-size external proxy. No print job was submitted.
connected_rdp_recheck_p24.delivery: Verification and documentation only. No binary rebuild or republish. The temporary sources, resources and executables were removed. This leaves native PrintDlgEx General and caller property pages as well as the administrator tray end-to-end check unverified.

print_general_feasibility_p25.native_option: The documented PD_USELARGETEMPLATE flag only changes the requested General template. An owned PrintDlgExW probe supplied a valid page-range buffer and PD_RETURNDC and requested its own additional page. Default and large General modes each timed out in native and published --2k on x86/x64, all 8 with the external zero-size proxy and zero caller-page create, init and release; the ordinary PropertySheetW controls all passed. No caller or system configuration was changed.
print_general_feasibility_p25.device_contract: A standalone native C17 probe used EnumPrintersW with PRINTER_ENUM_LOCAL, OpenPrinterW and DocumentPropertiesW. Both architectures discovered four local queues; all four on each width returned a valid driver DEVMODE through DM_OUT_BUFFER, accepted it back via DM_IN_BUFFER and returned the same public and private settings lengths. The test used application-owned buffers, closed all opened printer handles, and used neither DM_UPDATE nor a print job.
print_general_feasibility_p25.next_implementation: The native option does not provide the original General page on this host. The independently verified spooler calls can back an application-owned stock General presentation integrated with the existing print result transaction. Driver preference UI, live selection, Apply and caller property pages still require separate evidence. No product source or published binary changed; all temporary probes were removed.

places_reflow_trial.package: P9 published launcher and DLLs with temporary caller-owned ANSI and Unicode OPENFILENAME hooks. The probe used the ordinary desktop and owned dialogs at 96 DPI with a 427 by 272 work area. The temporary sources, objects, binaries and output were removed after the run.
places_reflow_trial.stock_geometry: The native 421 by 247 client exposed the stock Places toolbar, a Shell directory view, and a ComboBoxEx filename field. In Open the default OK button began at (484,313), beyond both client bounds.
places_reflow_trial.before_navigation: In a separate x64 trial, all four A/W open and save dialogs fit the directory view, filename edit, both action buttons and the five Places item rectangles. All four returned the expected file, filter index and offsets. The temporary driver reported failure because the stock caller hook intentionally bypassed its compact production-layout assertion.
places_reflow_trial.navigation: Sent button-down and button-up messages to the fourth item in the owned native Places toolbar. The current folder PIDL changed and the owned filename could be entered in all eight A/W open and save cases across x86 and x64. The expected file, filter and offsets were returned in six cases. Both x86 Open cases closed without selecting a file and reported zero extended error. The cached directory-view handle did not yield an in-bounds rectangle after navigation in any case. Buttons, filename field and all five toolbar item bounds still fit.
places_reflow_trial.native_control_p12: The same published package, viewport, hook and toolbar action were tested with the layout changes disabled and enabled. Native Places navigation replaced the directory HWND in 16/16. Reacquiring it showed the new view outside the client for all eight controls and inside it for all eight reflow cases. Opening an absolute filename directly from the virtual folder failed in two x86 controls and one x86 reflow case; x64 returned the expected file in all eight combined cases. The x86 failure therefore also occurs without reflow.
places_reflow_trial.filesystem_return_p12: After the Places action, a second probe entered the owned fixture directory, checked that the current Shell PIDL resolved back to that filesystem directory, and entered the relative filename there. Reflow preserved the file path, filter, offsets and working directory in 8/8 on x86/x64 A/W open/save. The unmodified control passed 7/8; one x86 ANSI Open did not observe the directory return within the bounded check. This does not determine the cause of that intermittent control failure.
places_reflow_trial.dropdown_extents_p12: A separate 8/8 reflow run preserved measured list-window heights for the filename history (219 px), filter (132 px), and drive combo (450 px) before and after placement. This covers native extent retention, not visible menu interaction. All three current diagnostic scratch directories were removed.
places_reflow_trial.repeated_resize_p13: At the measured 96 DPI, the 427 by 272 outer window used 38-pixel Places rows for the installed 32-pixel images and 13-pixel text metrics. At 411 by 256 the fifth row no longer fit in any of the eight A/W open/save cases. Returning to 427 by 272 restored the row rectangles. The directory view, filename field and two action buttons fit throughout, and two round trips through the virtual folder preserved selection in 8/8. The row dimensions do not support using this compressed layout as the product default.
places_reflow_trial.reference_size_p13: Mapped the SP2 1552 resource dimensions (370 by 197 DLU) using the native dialog's font. On the same ordinary desktop, forced only the owned probe dialog to the resulting 555 by 320 client, which exceeded the screen work area. With Places row height refreshed after each native resize, 8/8 retained the five row rectangles (52 pixels per row, 49 at the 539 by 304 test size), directory view, filename and action controls through two shrink/restore cycles and two navigations back to the fixture directory. The selected file, offsets, filter and working directory passed in 8/8. Cleanup removed the repeat, toolbar and reference-size probe directories.
places_reflow_trial.pending: The original-size trial establishes owned-window geometry, not measured operation on a larger physical desktop or a full Win2000 visual match. Real toolbar and dropdown rendering, product selection of the native Places host, and preserving row fit over native resize remain open. Keep the published compact variant for the small work area.

places_integration_p14.production: Eligible full-size Explorer single-file requests use the installed native Places host if the DPI-normalized work area is at least 565 by 345. The private form callback selects that standard host without forwarding synthetic flags to the caller. Layout takes 370 by 197 dialog units from the SP2 1552 reference. Native view and input controls remain in place as Windows controls; the observer updates the Places rows after native resizing. Caller hooks or templates, multiselect, and unsupported extended flags take the existing fallback. Compact work areas continue using the existing no-Places path.
places_integration_p14.real_work_area_incremental: Without a work-area override, tested the incremental candidate in a transient package on the current ordinary desktop at 427 by 272 and 96 DPI. File accept 16/16 including eight measured compact Explorer calls; cancel 16/16; insufficient buffers 8/8. The initial fixture tried flag equality even for the untouched old-style path and observed native flag updates. The assertion is confined to the two adapted Explorer paths.
places_integration_p14.large_area_integration: A transient adapter redirected only the work-area query to 720 by 480, with the product selection, reflow and resize observer compiled as implemented. It did not change the display configuration. x86/x64 A/W Win32 open/save passed 8/8 with native Places navigation, two shrink/restore cycles, two directory round trips, and exact file, filter and offset results. COM open/save confirmation and cancellation passed 8/8 and each observed a 555 by 320 Places client.
places_integration_p14.rendering: With the same synthetic work area, PrintWindow on the owned rendered toolbar detected colored upper pixels and dark lower pixels in all five rows, on both x86 and x64 at 96 DPI. This is window rendering into a local bitmap; it does not verify actual physical input, fullscreen desktop visibility, pixel identity with the original, or other DPI values. The temporary integration, paint and incremental candidate files were removed.

compact_explorer_p9.reference: Windows 2000 SP2 has two native Explorer templates, including 1547 without a Places toolbar. The Windows 11 no-Places path in both widths still uses SHELLDLL_DefView and a native ComboBoxEx32 filename edit.
compact_explorer_p9.behavior: For a full-size OPENFILENAME Explorer request with no caller hook, template, or multiselect, choose the stock compact variant when the work area can fit it and falls short of the Places layout envelope. The caller's structure and protocol options are preserved across the native call. Native Shell view, filter and selection are retained. The COM single-file bridge uses the same Win32 path.
compact_explorer_p9.fit: At 96 DPI with a 427 by 272 work area, the unadjusted compact Save window measured 436 by 306. Resizing the stock window after it initializes lets its own WM_SIZE handler place the directory view, filename edit, confirm and cancel controls inside the work area. Both the open and save outer bounds then fit 427 by 272.
compact_explorer_p9.scope: The wider Places layout, caller customization, multiselect and smaller work areas use the existing native flow. The metric decision is DPI-normalized; the 427 by 272 at 96 DPI runtime was the measured positive case. A full Places-layout visual match remains outstanding.
compact_explorer_p9.incremental: P5 failed the compact assertion in all eight measured A/W open/save geometry checks. The rebuilt candidate passed Win32 confirmation 16/16 (eight compact and eight legacy), cancellation 16/16, file buffer errors 8/8, and COM and Win16 comparisons 18/18. The 8/8 compact confirmations included preserved caller flags, correct filename and filter output, and unchanged working directory.
